_meta.purpose: Expert-rated ground truth for lib/racketFit.ts. Each case is a real (anonymised) or stringer-hypothetical member: their gear doc shape, their raw check-in ratings, and the set of rackets the owner and the club stringer agreed are ACCEPTABLE picks (a set, not one) plus any that would be plainly wrong. The test asserts the engine's top three intersects `acceptable` and avoids `unacceptable`. Populated by hand from `scripts/dump-fit-cases.mjs` skeletons (Phase 3); ids are gNN and carry no names. `ratedBy` says who rated it — mark hypotheticals honestly.
_meta.howToAdd: Copy a case, set gear.items[].catalogId to real catalog ids (the test refuses an id the catalog does not have), fill acceptable/unacceptable, set ratedBy and ratedAt.
_meta.pending: A case with `pending: true` is a DRAFT nobody has rated: the harness prints the engine's current top three beside its `acceptable` list for the owner and the stringer to confirm or correct, and asserts nothing about agreement. It does not count toward the kill criterion's five. Flip `pending` off and set `ratedBy` / `ratedAt` once a person has confirmed it.
_meta.manufacturer: A case with `rater: 'manufacturer'` is a SECOND OPINION, not expert truth: the brand's own series positioning (Yonex: Astrox = power / head-heavy, Nanoflare = speed / head-light, Arcsaber = control / even; Victor: Thruster = power, Auraspeed = speed, DriveX = all-round; Li-Ning: Axforce = power, Bladex = speed, Halbertec = control) turned into the acceptable set for a player type the brand describes. Marketing, so it is counted apart from the owner's and the stringer's cases and never toward the kill criterion's five; it is asserted like them because a disagreement with every brand at once is worth a red test.

cases.source: Badminton Performance Science deck (AI-generated, 2026-10-09), 'The developing player'
cases.note: Slow swing, beginner, doubles, wants deeper clears and forgiveness. Even balance and a flexible-to-medium shaft, light, at the slow tension band. Head-heavy frames are wrong for this swing: they add smash power only to a swing fast enough to accelerate them, and at this pace the power comes from the shaft and the string bed. The engine (fit-2) answered more_power with a head-heavy step and picked the Astrox 88 Play; fit-3 takes that step off for a slow swing because of this case.
cases.ratedBy: Grant (owner and club stringer), confirming the deck's prescription against the published buying guides ("I agree with online")

cases.source: Badminton Performance Science deck (AI-generated, 2026-10-09), 'The fast-twitch tactician'
cases.note: Doubles front-court player, medium swing, plays an even mid-range frame (ArcSaber 11 Play, Medium flex) and wants it faster in hand. The deck prescribes a head-light (low MOI) frame, a thin string and a medium tension. VERIFIED ONLINE 2026-10-09 (Grant: "use researching online to verify"): the Nanoflare 700 Pro / 700 Tour are head-light, Medium, sold for doubles front-court and flat exchanges; the Nextage is head-light, medium-ish, for intermediates; the 1000 Play is the same shape at an entry price. Two rows were DROPPED from the draft: the Auraspeed 90K is head-light but STIFF and sold for experienced/top players, a big step from a Medium beginner frame on a medium swing; the Bladex 700 is head-light Medium in 4U and head-heavy Stiff in 5U (retailers disagree), so it cannot be rated by name. Tension 24-25 lb matches the published intermediate ranges (23-25, 24-26).
cases.ratedBy: Grant (owner and club stringer), on the lists verified against published reviews ("02 and 03 looks good for now")

cases.source: Badminton Performance Science deck (AI-generated, 2026-10-09), 'The power smasher'
cases.note: Fast swing, advanced, doubles rear court, plays an Astrox 88D Pro and wants more power still. The deck prescribes a head-heavy (high MOI) stiff frame, a hybrid string and a high tension. VERIFIED ONLINE 2026-10-09: the Astrox 99 Pro (both generations) is the documented power upgrade from the 88D Pro (stiff, head-heavy, 2G-Namd in frame and shaft, needs a fast arm); the Thruster Ryuga II and Ryuga II Pro are head-heavy stiff smash frames (~295 mm); the Astrox 100ZZ is head-heavy extra-stiff for players who already swing fast. DROPPED from the draft: the 88S Pro and 88S Pro 3rd gen are the FRONT-COURT sibling of the 88D (lighter at the top, built for drives and interceptions), not a rear-court power step; the 3D Calibar 900 (non-Combat) is the milder 303 mm version and the catalog labels it Speed — the Combat is the power one and is not in the catalog. Tension 26-27 lb matches the published advanced/fast-swing ranges (26-28, 26-29).
cases.ratedBy: Grant (owner and club stringer), on the lists verified against published reviews ("02 and 03 looks good for now")
